items.title: Ajeet Bharti invoked caste superiority with the aim to humiliate Chandrashekhar Azad: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday held that remarks made by YouTuber Ajeet Bharti against Dalit leader and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad amounted to abuse using caste names and were intended to humiliate him. Justice Saurabh Banerjee returned the prima facie finding while denying Bharti anticipatory bail in the case under Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act [SC/ST Act]. The judge examined the video and its transcript containing the offending remarks by Bharti. The Court said that the YouTuber repeatedly invoked caste identity and ideas of caste superiority and that his statement cannot be said to be general or reckless/stray remarks. "They were clear references to caste, and explicit invocation of ideas of caste superiority prevalent in society, that too, with reference to the institution of marriage, which also represents age old notions of the hierarchy of the castes," the Court said. Justice Banerjee referred to Bharti's remark that Azad would have to “make himself worthy enough” to seek the hand of a “savarna” woman and said the remark “otherised” Azad, suggesting caste hierarchy and superiority. items.title: Calcutta High Court grants relief to ABP editor, journalist in FIR over ‘Gerua Gundami’ headline
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Thursday granted interim relief to the editor and a journalist of Anandabazar Patrika (ABP) from coercive action in a First Information Report (FIR) registered against them over the newspaper's use of the expression “Gerua Gundami” (Saffron Hooliganism) in a news headline [Ishani Datta Ray & Anr. v The State of West Bengal & Ors.] . The newspaper had used the expression to describe violence that unfolded at the Jadavpur University on August 20. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya granted interim relief to the accused after noting that the journalists had appeared before the police in response to notices issued during the investigation and had complied with them. During the hearing, the State also submitted that custodial interrogation of the journalists was not required. Taking note of the submissions, the Court directed the police not to take coercive action. "Concerned police authorities are directed not to take coercive steps against petitioners till 15th December, 2026 or until further order, whichever is earlier. items.title: Supreme Court commutes death sentence of man convicted of raping, killing 6-year-old stepdaughter
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday commuted the death sentence of a man convicted of repeatedly raping and murdering his 6-year-old stepdaughter. [Waris v. State of Madhya Pradesh] A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Vijay Bishnoi upheld his conviction but ordered that he spend the remainder of his natural life in prison, without remission. The Court found that the convict had killed the child to silence her and conceal the sexual assault. It described this as an aggravating circumstance “of the highest order”, but said the gravity of the crime could not, by itself, establish that he was beyond reform. “A crime may be exceptionally grave and its perpetrator may yet not be shown to be beyond reform, and where that is so the law, as it has recently been applied, does not exact his life ,” the Court said. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Vijay Bishnoi The Bench noted that convict had no criminal antecedents, his conduct in custody had been satisfactory and the State had led no evidence that he was incapable of reform. items.title: P&H High Court cancels murder accused's bail after his 'band baja dunga' threat
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has cancelled the bail granted to a murder accused after he sent various threatening messages to the complainant and his family, including one saying "band baja dunga" [Sourabh Narula v State of Haryana & Anr] Justice Vikram Aggarwal said the accused cannot be permitted to remain on bail because any untoward incident can take place if he is allowed to remain free. "In the considered opinion of this Court, he has violated the most essential condition of the order granting bail by threatening the complainant side," the Court said. Justice Vikram Aggarwal The accused Suresh alias Binni Sardana is accused of having committed the murder of one Shyam Lal, who was the servant of one Mukul, a cousin of the complainant Sourabh Narula. Suresh was granted bail on January 28 by the High Court in the case dating back to June 24, 2023. However, soon after he came out of the prison, the accused allegedly started threatening the accused. Narula then moved the Court. In his petition, the complainant said that he and his father received threatening messages on Instagram and Facebook from the accused. One message to the complainant's sister was flagged in particular.

items.title: Air India fined ₹50k for de-boarding disabled woman, damaging wheelchair
items.summary: The Court of the Chief Commissioner for Persons With Disabilities (CCPD court) recently imposed a ₹50,000 fine on Air India for regulatory violations, apart from recommending that it pay ₹5 lakhs as compensation to a disabled woman for de-boarding her from the plane without reasons. The order was passed on September 24 by the Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities S Govindaraj on a complaint by Falguni Maheshwari. Maheshwari, a wheelchair-bound woman with 80 percent locomotor disability, flew from Frankfurt to India in May 2026 on an Air India flight. However, she was de-boarded from a connecting flight that was to take her from Delhi to Bhuj without providing any written reasons. The complainant also alleged that her wheelchair was returned in a damaged condition. She stated that she was forced to arrange alternative flights at her own expense under severe emotional distress. Air India stated that de-planing the woman regulatory necessity solely on safety grounds. It stated that at the time of boarding, the woman was displaying certain medical concerns. items.title: Karnataka High Court quashes criminal case against shopkeeper accused of insulting PM Narendra Modi
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a shopkeeper booked for using insulting words against Prime Minister Narendra Modi [Imtiyaz Nuruddin Chinchali v State of Karnataka]. Justice Venkatesh Naik T found that the allegations against the shopkeeper were general and omnibus in nature. "There is no specific allegation that the petitioner abused or intentionally insulted the complainant so as to provoke a breach of peace," the Court said. The Court also said there was a delay of four days in lodging the complaint. It added that since no offences were made out in the case, continuation of proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of law. Justice Venkatesh Naik T Athani police station in Belagavi had registered the case in January on the basis of a video of the incident involving shopkeeper Imtiyaz Nuruddin Chinchali. The accused on the date of incident had allegedly used insulting words against the Prime Minister after he was questioned about the barricades placed by him outside his shop. items.title: Supreme Court dismisses PIL for use of Hindi as one of its official court languages
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking directions for the constitution of a commission to examine the possible use of Hindi as an official language of the Court. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that such measures cannot be introduced through judicial orders. “These things do not happen through court orders. They happen as part of reforms, slowly and in a phased manner. Such things we are doing,” said CJI Kant. CJI Kant also pointed out that the Supreme Court has been introducing services that gradually incorporate the use of regional languages. "We are now giving a brief description of all the reports in Hindi. We will start with other regional languages. We will maintain the culture. We will respect other regional languages also,” he said. items.title: Litigant can't disown lawyer's arguments to wriggle out of orders: Delhi High Court
items.summary: A litigant cannot back out of orders passed on the strength of submissions made by its own counsel by later claiming that the lawyer lacked instructions or authority, the Delhi High Court has held [ Equitas Small Finance Bank Ltd vs Nirmala Bai Shanthilal & Ors. ] Justice Saurabh Banerjee made the observation while dismissing a writ petition filed by Equitas Small Finance Bank seeking to set aside a September 2024 Lok Adalat award. By the said award, the Lok Adalat had permitted the settlement of a cheque bounce case filed against a borrower. In its writ petition, Equitas claimed that its lawyer had earlier wrongly submitted before the Lok Adalat that the dispute was settled. The bank alleged that the said submission was made under immense confusion and without authority. It, therefore, sought the recall of the Lok Adalat award. The High Court, however, refused to grant any such relief. It observed that permitting the bank to disown its lawyer’s earlier arguments could create chaos. "No litigant like the petitioner herein can be permitted to resile from order(s) passed on the strength of counsel’s submissions. items.title: Delhi High Court denies bail to man accused of raping women he met through fake matrimonial profiles
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently rejected the bail plea of a man accused of creating multiple fake profiles on matrimonial websites and inducing women into sexual relations on false promise of marriage [ Gaurav Jaiswal Vs The State ]. The Court observed that the accused had created 9 fake profiles on the matrimonial website, carrying varying personal and professional details. It noted that one fake profile was made in the name of a girl. In the verdict delivered on September 22, Justice Girish Kathpalia observed that prima facie , the Court agrees with the prosecution that the man is a “predator of innocent girls”. “Those profiles are of different ranges of age, different ranges of qualification and different ranges of occupation/income, which prima facie lends credence to the argument of learned ASC that the accused/applicant is a predator of innocent girls,” the Court stated. items.title: Father facing POCSO prosecution not entitled to child's custody: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a father facing prosecution under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act) for sexual abuse of his son cannot be given custody of his children. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said that if the son is handed over to the father, the possibility of the son giving a free and fair deposition in the POCSO proceedings would virtually be negligible. "Under no circumstances, the respondent-father, as long as he is facing prosecution, can be considered to be a person entitled to custody of the children," the Court said. The Court was hearing appeals by the mother against a Delhi High Court judgment which had upheld a family court's decision to grant father the sole custody of the couple's two children, aged about 13 and 7. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The couple married in 2011. The wife left the matrimonial home in 2018 when she was pregnant. She alleged physical assault. Since then, she has had custody of their son and of their daughter, who was born in 2019.
